guest.bio_context: Cole Lindberg started working at Worlds of Fun in Kansas City, Missouri as a summer job at age 14, wearing a suit to his interview. Eleven years later, he became a full-time year-round employee running the park's entire games department, overseeing 32 games and supervising over 100 young employees. In his senior year at the University of Kansas at Lawrence, he dropped out of school to accept the games manager position, describing it as 'probably only going to come along once in a lifetime.' His immediate boss Matt considers him one of the best games managers among the 11 amusement parks owned by Cedar Fair.

pending_qa.q: What is the business logic behind letting players win prizes at amusement park games even when the game operator guesses wrong?
pending_qa.r: At Worlds of Fun, the guessing game costs $5 to play while the prizes cost less than $5, meaning the department makes a profit even if every single guess is wrong. Cole actively encourages intentional wrong guesses because players carrying prizes around the park serve as walking advertisements for all the games. This turns prize giveaways into a marketing strategy rather than a loss.

pending_qa.q: How did Cole Lindberg use prize selection and game design to increase revenue at Worlds of Fun?
pending_qa.r: Cole introduced a fluorescent-colored lemur stuffed animal as a prize in the dart game, and the game doubled its business as a result. He also invented a game called Pigs of Fury — a giant slingshot where players launch bean bags at pigs — which became one of the top-performing games in the park. His approach treats prize selection and game presentation as core revenue drivers, not afterthoughts.

pending_qa.q: What is Cedar Fair and how does Worlds of Fun fit within its portfolio of amusement parks?
pending_qa.r: Cedar Fair is a company that owns 11 amusement parks and six water parks, with Worlds of Fun in Kansas City, Missouri being one of its properties. Cole knows the games department managers at the other Cedar Fair parks and notes that while some do employee competitions, none go as far as Worlds of Fun does. However, Worlds of Fun is described as one of the smallest of the 11 parks in Cedar Fair's portfolio.

pending_qa.q: Why do seasonal workers keep returning to Worlds of Fun year after year despite the demanding conditions?
pending_qa.r: Multiple employees, including Claire (in her third year at age 18) and Sam (in his third summer), stated explicitly that Cole Lindberg is the reason they keep coming back. Claire pointed to events like Rally Days, Deathmatch, Sweet Sixteen, and Toss the Boss as the things that keep the job exciting through the season. Sam described Cole as someone who 'was made to do this,' noting that even goofy acts like singing at morning meetings feel natural and right rather than awkward.
